post.summary: Click-to-call: Twilio rings your phone (`agent_phone`), then the contact's number from the workspace's caller ID. Refused with a reason when phone calls are off, Twilio is not connected, the contact has no number or has not agreed to be called on it (`NO_CALL_CONSENT`), opted out (`DO_NOT_CALL`), is in a country that is not allowed or has a premium-rate number (`DESTINATION_BLOCKED`), it is night for the visitor (`QUIET_HOURS`), or a limit is reached (`DAILY_LIMIT`, per-agent hourly limit)
Ask the visitor, with a form card in the thread, to confirm their number and agree to be called on it

Tap a quick reply under a bot message (`Yes, thanks` resolves the ticket, `Not quite` lets the AI agent try again or hand over, `Talk to a person`, a department). The tap is stored as the visitor's message; a card can be tapped once (`409 ALREADY_ANSWERED`)

"Talk to a person": always available, whether or not an AI agent exists. Stores the request and hands the ticket off through the department's routing; repeating it while a person has the ticket changes nothing
Thumbs up (1) or down (-1) on an AI answer

Answer a form card the server put in the thread (name, email, phone, custom fields, consent). Validated here: email syntax, phone parsed to E.164 with the picked `country`, name charset; `422 INVALID_FORM` with per-field `errors`; a card is answered once (`409 ALREADY_ANSWERED`). An email or phone that already belongs to another contact is kept as unverified and never merges that contact's history
Skip an optional form card (`422 NOT_SKIPPABLE` when it has a required field)
Send a one-time code to verify the visitor
Verify the one-time code
